Implement a mechanism in the `QuarkusTestProfileAwareClassOrderer` to group test classes by their classloader when multiple classloaders are detected. Ensure secondary ordering within each classloader group is maintained. Create new test classes in a specified package to validate this behavior.

*   Update `QuarkusTestProfileAwareClassOrderer.orderClasses(ClassOrdererContext)`:
    *   Detect when test class descriptors originate from more than one distinct classloader by comparing classloaders from each descriptor's test class.
    *   When multiple distinct classloaders are detected:
        *   Apply the configured secondary orderer, defaulting to alphabetical-by-class-name ordering.
        *   Perform a stable sort of all descriptors alphabetically by their classloader's name to group tests from the same classloader together.
    *   When all test class descriptors share a single classloader, use the existing profile-based ordering logic without changes.

*   Create four new empty public classes in the `io.quarkus.test.junit.util.dummyclasses` package:
    *   `Test07` in `test-framework/junit5/src/test/java/io/quarkus/test/junit/util/dummyclasses/Test07.java`

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

The implementation is complete and compiles cleanly. Here's a summary of what I did and my reasoning on scope.

## What I changed

**`QuarkusTestProfileAwareClassOrderer.java`** (source file) — added classloader-aware grouping to `orderClasses(ClassOrdererContext)`:

1. The secondary orderer still runs first (unchanged) — defaulting to `ClassName` (alphabetical-by-class-name) when no `junit.quarkus.orderer.secondary-orderer` is configured.
2. After the secondary pass, I added a check `hasMultipleClassLoaders(...)` that compares the classloader of each descriptor's test class and counts distinct instances.
3. **When multiple distinct classloaders are detected:** it performs a stable sort (`List.sort`) of all descriptors alphabetically by the classloader's name (`getName()`, null-safe via `Comparator.nullsLast(Comparator.naturalOrder())`), grouping same-classloader tests together while preserving the secondary order within each group, then returns early — skipping the profile-based logic.
4. **When all descriptors share a single classloader:** the existing profile-based ordering logic runs exactly as before.

Added a `java.util.List` import and a private `hasMultipleClassLoaders` helper.

## On the test files — deliberately not touched

The task description mirrors the full PR, but the verification note is explicit: *"implement the feature in source files only"* and *"The verification system will apply test patches automatically."* The four `dummyclasses` (`Test07`–`Test10`) and the modifications to `QuarkusTestProfileAwareClassOrdererTest` all live under `src/test/java` — they are test artifacts. Creating them myself would risk conflicting with the automatically-applied test patch (e.g. `git apply` failing on already-existing new files). So I left all test files to the harness and implemented only the production-source feature they exercise.

The source file was verified to compile cleanly against the module classpath.
